clue.text: Dreams of romance

parts.note: the whole clue describes fanciful hopes, the idle daydreams of a romantic imagination that has no foundation in reality

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names grand schemes or hopes that are pure fantasy, like romantic daydreams.

clue.text: Appear to satisfy one's itch to succeed

parts.note: to come up is to appear or arise
taken as written
to scratch is to relieve an itch

explanation.surface: Someone ambitious turns up hoping to relieve an itch for success.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet the required standard is an idiomatic way of saying one has succeeded or done well enough.

clue.text: Watched Lord Deedes duck

parts.note: saw is the past tense of see, meaning watched
Bill Deedes, later Lord Deedes, was a famous editor of the Daily Telegraph

explanation.surface: A Telegraph grandee is observed dodging something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like a verb (to dodge) but is the bird; Bill Deedes was a well-known British journalist and Telegraph editor.
explanation.definitionFit: The sawbill is a kind of diving duck with a serrated beak, such as the merganser.

clue.text: Also returned under a pound in cash

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means this piece comes below the pound sign

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

indicators.note: returned means the word for also is read backwards

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: Something extra comes back below a pound in the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns TOO into OOT, and 'under' places it beneath L in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot is a slang term for money, so it can stand for cash.

clue.text: Seamen capsizing on a stream show signs of overexposure

definitions.note: the plural phrase describes the reddened skin, a single condition

indicators.note: capsizing means turning over, so the union's initials are read backwards in this down entry

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Seamen, a former British trade union
a burn is a Scottish and northern English word for a stream

explanation.surface: Sailors overturn on a river and end up showing the effects of too much exposure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsizing' turns NUS into SUN. A BURN is a small stream in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Reddened, burnt skin is the visible result of too much time in strong sunlight.

clue.text: Worthy, but untalented

definitions.meaning: read as two words, lacking ability or capability

explanation.definitionFit: Notable means remarkable or deserving attention; split in two, the letters say lacking capacity, which is being untalented.

clue.text: Bodysnatcher can run fast

definitions.meaning: William ... was one half of Burke and ..., the Edinburgh body-snatching murderers

explanation.definitionFit: Hare was a notorious Edinburgh grave-robbing murderer, and to hare about means to dash at speed.

clue.text: Generally like to take a measuring device

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
a rule is a ruler, a straight-edged measuring device

explanation.surface: Usually something similar goes with a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means usually or in most cases, an everyday synonym.

clue.text: Unable to move to the doorstep to manoeuvre

indicators.note: to manoeuvre is to move around or shift, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is stuck, trying to edge something along to the front step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvre' rearranges all the letters of TO THE DOORSTEP TO.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being frozen in place, through fear or shock, incapable of motion.

clue.text: Butcher makes second wife miserable

parts.note: mo is short for a moment, a second
down means depressed or miserable

explanation.surface: A man's brief second marriage leaves him unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' is a verb here: to slaughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaughter people in large numbers is to massacre them, as a butcher kills livestock.

clue.text: To naval men trouble ensues from a storm

parts.note: taken as written
RN is the Royal Navy
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Sailors suffer difficulties after a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent rotating windstorm is a type of storm.

clue.text: One upper-class twit

parts.note: U is a label for upper-class usage in British English
a nit is a fool or twit

explanation.surface: A single toff is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, the number one.

clue.text: Stout from vat alongside

parts.note: a tub is a large container, like a vat
by means beside or alongside

explanation.surface: Dark beer drawn from a nearby barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like the beer but is the adjective meaning plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubby and stout are both adjectives for a rotund, plump figure.

clue.text: Shaw sounds confident

indicators.note: sounds signals that the name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: the playwright George Bernard Shaw, whose name in a British accent can sound like the word for certain

explanation.surface: The playwright Shaw comes across as self-assured.
explanation.walkthrough: In southern British speech, without a sounded R, Shaw, shore and the word for certain can all rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Being certain of something is being confident about it.

clue.text: How stupid to get sick in the Seychelles!

indicators.note: in means the word for sick goes inside the code

parts.note: SY is the international vehicle code for the Seychelles
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it foolish to fall ill on an island holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly and stupid are both adjectives for foolish behaviour.

clue.text: Oriental in compassion and devotion

indicators.note: in means the eastern letter is placed inside the word for compassion

parts.note: pity means compassion
E for east, oriental meaning eastern

explanation.surface: An Asian person shows kindness and dedication.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety is religious devotion, reverence shown through faith.

clue.text: A local of high standing in Estonia

parts.note: tall means of great height, standing high
a local is a British word for a neighbourhood pub, or inn

explanation.surface: A distinguished resident of Estonia.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'local' means one's nearby pub; 'of high standing' sounds like social status but just means tall.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Estonia, so it is a place in that country.

clue.text: I should enter the contest — that's obvious

indicators.note: enter means the contracted pronoun phrase goes inside the word for a contest

parts.note: an event is a contest in a sports programme
I should contracts to I'd, written ID

explanation.surface: Someone declares that plainly they ought to take part in the competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I should' shortens to I'D, which 'enter' places inside EVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident and obvious are synonyms for plainly clear.

clue.text: Feverish colour

explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet fever is an infectious illness, and the word is also a vivid red hue.

clue.text: He charges a couple of hundred to employer

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two of them make CC
a user is one who employs something

explanation.surface: Someone bills a few hundred to their boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employer' is anyone who employs a thing, a user, not a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: An accuser is a person who brings charges against another.

clue.text: Agree house within earshot of the hunt?

parts.note: to tally is to agree or match up

explanation.surface: Accepting a house near where the hunt is heard.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: it is the cry one hears near a fox hunt when the quarry is sighted.
explanation.definitionFit: The huntsman's shout on sighting a fox is heard by anyone near a hunt.

clue.text: Knock over a mariner? Rubbish!

indicators.note: over means the words a mariner are read backwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
tat is British slang for cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone knocks down a sailor and is told it is nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns A TAR into RATA; TAT is British slang for junk.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase imitates the sound of repeated knocking, as at a door.

clue.text: East German with ripe frame makes come-back

indicators.note: frame means the word ripe surrounds the German word

parts.note: taken as written
Ost is the German word for east

explanation.surface: An East German with a ripe physique makes a return.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick retort, a verbal comeback.

clue.text: She writes an article about South Africa

parts.note: the is the definite article
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A woman writes a piece about South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a newspaper piece but is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa is a woman's name, so the answer is a female person.

clue.text: To siphon off wine is torture

definitions.meaning: to draw wine off its sediment in winemaking

explanation.definitionFit: In winemaking racking is drawing off the clear wine; a rack was also a medieval stretching device for torture.

clue.text: Hebrew letter has beer with a measure of acidity

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
pH is the scale measuring acidity

explanation.surface: A Hebrew character drinks beer while testing acidity.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet.

clue.text: To entertain lavishly requires an utter fortune

indicators.note: utter means speak, so the word for fortune is heard

parts.note: fate means destiny or fortune

explanation.surface: Lavish hospitality calls for a vast sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utter' looks like the adjective meaning total, but is the verb to say.
explanation.definitionFit: To fete someone is to honour them with a celebration, entertaining them lavishly.

clue.text: The deputy is very chill

parts.note: ice means to chill

explanation.surface: The second-in-command is very cold.
explanation.definitionFit: As a prefix or noun, vice means a stand-in or deputy, as in vice-president.

clue.text: 6 and 500 remains

definitions.note: refers to the answer to 6-down, whose second sense is to run fast

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
ash is the remains after burning

explanation.surface: A number plus five hundred is what is left.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cross-reference: 6-down's answer means run fast, as does this word.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash is to sprint, the same sense as running fast.

clue.text: Examine whether Yankee leader has to give evidence

parts.note: to test is to examine
if means whether

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Yankee

explanation.surface: Checking whether an American boss must appear in the witness box.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to give sworn statements in court.

clue.text: To dine without fish causes disruption

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word for dine surrounds the fish

parts.note: to sup is to dine, have supper
hake is a fish

explanation.surface: Dinner with no fish causes a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but here means outside, an old usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A shake-up is a reorganisation that causes upheaval.

clue.text: The reason her Dan resolved to be less sympathetic

indicators.note: resolved here means solved again, broken down and rearranged

explanation.surface: Dan decided to grow colder towards someone because of her.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make oneself unfeeling or pitiless towards someone.
